$comment: ANTI-mirror map for backend/system <-> frontend/lib/system (openspec:
pin-system-generation-determinism, design.md Decision 5 — `system` is
designated Go-sole-authority for interior generation, and shipped
cross-stack-determinism binds that designation to an anti-mirror check:
'A mirror map for a capability designated Go-sole-authority (no
TypeScript mirror) SHALL instead run in anti-mirror mode: it SHALL fail
if any function name is declared in both the Go package and the
designated non-mirror TypeScript directory, unless that name appears in
an explicit, empty-by-default sharedNames allowlist recorded in the
pair's mirror-map file.'
This is `backend/space`'s SECOND anti-mirror sibling (fixtures/space/
mirror-map.json is the first) — same shape, same rationale: there is
deliberately no 'pairs' array, because a pairs entry would assert the
very mirror this designation forbids.
'sharedNames' is empty BY DEFAULT and should stay that way.
frontend/lib/system does not exist (design.md Decision 5 / tasks.md
5.6): .claude/scripts/check-mirror-map.sh's generalized anti_mirror
function takes its existing directory-does-not-exist branch for the
'system' pass and prints a stated trivial pass — the same shape 'space'
had before frontend/lib/space existed. anti_mirror reads ONLY
'sharedNames' (never 'coverage' or 'inventory' — those are read by
check_mirror, which system has no 'pairs' for), and for 'system' it does
not read even that: the directory-absent branch returns before opening
this file at all. So 'coverage' and 'inventory' below are declared,
greppable documentation with a named owner, not an asserted check — the
day someone adds frontend/lib/system, this map (and the generalized
anti_mirror pass) is already watching.
'coverage' is this package's COVERAGE INVENTORY (design.md Decision 5 /
tasks.md 4.1b), scoped to the RULE-BEARING SURFACE ONLY: the functions
declared in generator.go, continuous.go, belt.go, bodies.go,
params_continuous.go (no functions of its own — constants/tables only),
and station_continuous.go. DAO, handler, service and generated-mock
functions are NOT rule-bearing and are out of scope for this list —
concretely, that excludes bodies.go's (*Service) methods (BodyTable,
addGates: Firestore/service orchestration), BodyTable's own pure
accessor methods (Body, StarId, StarSize, Extent, Ids: field getters,
not computed rules), and asDisclosureWorld (a compile-time-only
capability check with zero production callers, wrapping a pointer with
no computation of its own).
Values: 'family:<name>' — asserted by that family in
fixtures/system/cases.json, directly or indirectly as a callee of the
family's function; 'inventory' — no family exercises it, tracked as a
gap in 'inventory' below, each entry naming an owning change per the
shipped rule that a rule-bearing shared function SHALL NOT remain in the
inventory across more than one change that modifies its package.

inventory.why: Pure function of a continuous radius over its full R¹ domain; interiorElements exercises it only at the radii generation happens to produce (coverage, not a contract over the full box). Per the orchestrator's ruling (design.md Decision 5, Open Question 1), owned downstream rather than built out here for a fast-tracked determinism fix.

Pure function of two galaxy-tier coordinate pairs and a system's continuous Extent; no fixture family sweeps its input box (the bearing derivation via space.PhaseIndexOf, the fixed radius factor, the dz/dx horizontal-projection convention). Named explicitly in design.md Decision 5 as deferred.

Named 'stationOrbit' in design.md Decision 5: a pure function of the galaxy seed, system id, and skeleton, with its own parent-selection hash and type-keyed ceiling; no fixture family sweeps it, and its two callees (MaxFeatureSize, inclinationForDominant) are consequently uncovered too.

A deterministic string-format helper ("gate-" + destSystemId) with no floating-point or cross-target arithmetic content — not the kind of value this capability's fixture machinery exists to pin. Covered functionally by bodies_test.go, not by a byte-for-byte fixture family.
inventory.expectedChange: the change that first gives lane gates a fixture-worthy rule (e.g. a gate id format change) — until then this is a documentation gap, not a determinism risk
